title: Hosted Inference Surface: Pragmatic PRD for Generation + Retrieval Endpoints and Phased Rollout Checklist
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a pragmatic, single-surface product for hosted inference that bundles generation (chat / completions) and retrieval primitives (embeddings + rerank) into a cohesive developer experience. Goal is to ship a minimal, backward-compatible API surface that meets engineering SLOs, satisfies enterprise security constraints, and unlocks predictable unit economics for customers.

Objectives:
- Deliver a single, well-documented endpoint family for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank that is easy to adopt from SDKs and REST.
- Ensure non-disruptive rollout for existing hosted customers (no breaking changes to keys/URLs).
- Meet latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms for simple embeddings, p95 < 800ms for 256-token completions on dedicated tier.
- Provide clear fallbacks and routing for capacity-constrained regions.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not include multi-modal asset ingestion (images/audio) — that will be in a follow-up.
- No new billing model changes; we will reuse existing token-based and embedding-unit metrics for launch.

Public API contract (high-level):
- /v1/generate -> completions + streaming chat support with function calls and structured output hints.
- /v1/embeddings -> vector output, optional version tag for quantized models.
- /v1/rerank -> accepts candidate IDs + query, returns scored ranking + stable tie-breaker.
- All endpoints accept optional route metadata: model, region, session_id, deterministic (bool).

Key success metrics for launch:
- Adoption: 20% of active hosted API keys make at least one request to new surface within 30 days.
- Reliability: region-level downtime < 0.1% over first 90 days.
- Quality: average semantic similarity delta for migrated embedding requests within ±0.02 of baseline for top-10 recall test sets.

Audience & users:
- Primary: software and ML engineers embedding LLM features in product flows.
- Secondary: platform teams standardizing inference across services.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API stability and compatibility:
- Existing hosted endpoints remain reachable during rollout; redirect behavior validated for 1000 legacy keys in staging.
- Backwards-compatible request/response schema documented; SDKs map old calls to new routes without behavioral drift.

2) Performance & SLOs:
- p50/p90/p95 for completions and embeddings meet targets under 70th percentile workload from 30-day sample.
- Autoscaling and burst policies validate by synthetic load tests (scale up < 90s, scale down < 300s).

3) Observability & Tracing:
- Token-level cost breakdown available in Console per-route.
- End-to-end traces include model variant, kernel path, and cache hit/miss ratio.

4) Security & Compliance:
- Private deployment compatibility verified (VPC test harness).
- KMS integrations work for stored artifacts; all audit logs surface request and response hashes only (no raw prompt storage).

5) UX & Docs:
- Console view shows per-route latency, cost, and error breakdown.
- Quickstart guides + SDK snippets for Node/Python/Go published and reviewed.

6) Regression safety:
- Eval-driven quality gates: no regression > 1.5% in top-line QA prompts; automatic rollback configured on regression detection.

7) Operational runbook & rollback:
- Runbook covering canary thresholds, rollback steps, and fallback to compatible model variants is approved by SRE and PM.
rollout_checklist:
Phase 0 — Pre-launch (gated)
- Confirm schema compatibility tests pass for legacy client bindings (ENG).
- Security review sign-off and KMS test artifacts (Sec & Infra).
- Finalize traffic-splitting policy and default fallback model (PM + SRE).
- Publish developer docs + migration guide in Confluence.

Phase 1 — Canary (internal + partner customers)
- Release endpoint to 2 internal tenants and 5 partner keys. Run 7-day smoke tests for functionality and SLOs.
- Monitor telemetry for cache hit ratio, latency, error rates, and cost per token.
- Collect API ergonomics feedback from SDK users; triage non-blocking UX items.

Phase 2 — Controlled ramp
- Gradually open to 5% of external keys by usage; run automation that looks for regressions across 10 eval prompt sets.
- Validate rollback automation and fallback model correctness.
- Create support playbook and add canned responses for the top 5 expected issues.

Phase 3 — Broad availability
- Announce GA with dedicated blog post, release notes, and SDK updates.
- Monitor first 72 hours aggressively with 15m on-call cadence and dedicated Slack channel.
- Post-launch review 14 days after GA to capture lessons and next-phase scope.
telemetry_and_slo:
Required metrics to instrument:
- Per-request: model_id, model_variant, kernel_type, sequence_length, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, route, region, customer_key_hash, cache_hit (bool), execution_ms.
- Aggregates: cost-per-token by model_variant, p50/p90/p95 latency by route and region, error rate by HTTP code and internal failure type.

SLOs at launch:
- Embeddings: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms (hosted tier).
- Completions: p50 < 220ms, p95 < 800ms (for 256 tokens).
- Rerank: p50 < 220ms, p95 < 600ms (10 candidates).

Alert thresholds:
- Error rate > 2% for 15m -> P0 alert.
- p95 latency > target * 1.5 for 10m -> investigate and scale.
- Quality regression detected by eval harness -> immediate canary hold and auto-rollback if above threshold.
qa_and_test_plan:
Automated tests:
- Contract tests for request/response shapes across language SDKs.
- Regression eval harness: 12 prompt suites covering generation coherence, hallucination rates, embedding similarity, and rerank precision.
- Load tests across regions: sustained 5k rps for small bursts, 1k sustained with mixture of routes.

Manual QA:
- Exploratory test pass by PM + Design focusing on structured output & function-calling experience.
- Security QA: attempt to exfiltrate sensitive content through prompts in staging; verify logging and redaction behavior.

Acceptance gating:
- All automated gates green for 48h on canary before moving to controlled ramp.
migration_and_backward_compatibility:
Strategy:
- Keep existing hosted endpoints live; new endpoints are additive. Provide server-side mapping so older SDK calls are routed to equivalent new route for 6 months.
- Deprecation policy: announce 90-day deprecation for old route aliases once adoption hits 50% of active keys.
- SDKs: ship shims in Node/Python/Go that map old method names to new route; ensure identical default parameters.

Edge cases & mitigation:
- If customers rely on undocumented behavior (e.g., exact whitespace tokenization differences), provide a compatibility toggle per-key to pin model variant.
- For enterprise customers on Dedicated, allow explicit model pinning and region reservation to avoid cross-region fallbacks.
